key_insight: Machine-learning models compress quantum measurement data to supply wavefunction overlaps efficiently, accelerating quantum-classical quantum Monte Carlo by orders of magnitude.
engineering_relevance: Reusing learned quantum-state information reduces repeated classical measurement-processing costs, addressing a scaling bottleneck in hybrid quantum simulation.
method: Prepare trial wavefunctions on a quantum processor to guide classical quantum Monte Carlo.
Compress quantum measurement data into machine-learning models.
Use the models to efficiently provide wavefunction overlaps during simulation.
evidence_signal: Using measurements from Google's Willow processor, the authors demonstrate hydrogen-chain and strongly correlated iron-sulfur-cluster simulations, reporting chemical accuracy on up to 40 qubits.
watch_item: Deployment should verify that learned overlap errors remain controlled for new systems and do not compromise final energy accuracy.
paper_title: Machine learning quantum data to accelerate quantum Monte Carlo
